text:
### Observed differences

- Five activities that were part of almost every trace earlier are now almost gone: in the earlier window A20, A21, A30, A31 and A32 each ran in about 199–200 of 200 traces — all five together in about 995 of 1000 traces, in varying order (A20 preceded A21 in about 49 in 100 traces and followed it in about 51 in 100) — whereas in the later window each appears in only 1–3 of 200 traces. [OCC003, OCC004, OCC009, OCC010, OCC011, REL040, REL083]

- In the later window, five largely new activities run instead: A19, A22, A23, A24 and A25, seen in 0–3 of 200 traces earlier, now each appear in about 32–49 of 200 traces (roughly 16–25 in 100). Any two of them share a trace in at most about 1 in 100 cases and their shares sum to about one execution per trace, so they behave as alternatives of which typically one runs. [OCC002, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, OCC008, REL033, REL059, REL067, REL074]

- The switch is located between A48 and A33. Earlier, about 95 in 100 of A48's outgoing transitions went to the old five activities (about 17–21 in 100 each), and each of them preceded A33 in about 97–99 in 100 of their joint appearances. In the later window, about 95 in 100 of A48's outgoing transitions go to the new five (about 14–23 in 100 each), the new activities lead back to A33 in about 89–100 in 100 of their outgoing transitions (A19 lowest at about 89, A22 at about 100), and A48 reaches A33 within two steps in about 94 in 100 of 199 later observations. [DIR012, REL048, REL049, REL057, REL085, REL088, REL090, REL091, DIR003, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008, REL081, LAG029]

- Event positions agree with a shorter segment: A33's mean position moved earlier (about 0.50 to 0.43 of the trace) and A48's slightly later (about 0.33 to 0.38), while the new activities sit at mean positions of about 0.40–0.43, close to where the old block used to sit (about 0.41–0.42); A15, A16, A33 and A48 themselves remained in every trace of both windows. [POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, POS007, POS008, POS009, POS010, POS011, POS012, POS013, POS014, POS015]

- Outside this segment, A04 became much more involved: it appears in about 67 of 200 later traces versus about 21 earlier; A15 now leads to A04 in about 17 in 100 of its outgoing transitions (about 1 in 100 earlier), A04 leads to A16 in about 85 in 100 (about 22 in 100 earlier), usually as the immediate next step (lag 1 in about 98 in 100 of 58 observations versus about 33 in 100 of 9 earlier), and A04's mean position moved earlier and much tighter (about 0.49 to 0.28, spread 0.35 to 0.18). [OCC001, DIR001, DIR002, LAG001, POS001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the five-activity block A20, A21, A30, A31 and A32, which ran in varying order between A48 and A33 in virtually every earlier trace, is no longer executed in the later window, and that instead a single activity chosen among five largely new alternatives — A19, A22, A23, A24 and A25 — runs between A48 and A33. The placement is shown directly by the successor profiles: A48's outgoing transitions moved wholesale from the old five (about 95 in 100) to the new five (about 95 in 100), the new activities lead on to A33, and A48 now reaches A33 in two steps in about 94 in 100 traces, whereas the old five previously sat between A48 and A33. Participation flipped from about 199–200 to 1–3 of 200 traces for the old five and from 0–3 to 32–49 for the new ones, while A15, A16, A33 and A48 stayed in every trace of both windows, confining the change to this segment. Screening qualified 158 control-flow items where about 1 would be expected without a change, so the pattern as a whole is not a sampling artefact, although many pair-level items restate the same block change rather than adding independent confirmation. [OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, OCC008, OCC009, OCC010, OCC011, REL048, REL049, DIR012, DIR003, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008, LAG029, POS002, POS003, POS014, POS015]

Limitations: the later-window picture of the old block rests on only 1–3 traces, so the evidence cannot distinguish a complete removal from a drop to rare, optional execution, nor whether the new alternatives are newly added activities or previously existing but rarely taken paths; the residual routing of the old activities in the later window is based on 1–3 observations each. [OCC003, OCC009, DIR004, DIR009, DIR010, DIR011]

Other differences: A04 participates far more often (about 34 in 100 later traces versus about 11 in 100 before) and its routing consolidated around A15 → A04 → A16, typically with A04 immediately before A16; its mean position moved earlier and much tighter. The before-side of this routing rests on only about 23 observed outgoing transitions of A04, so those earlier shares are imprecise. [OCC001, DIR001, DIR002, LAG001, POS001]
